          // Hide the bare auto-caption Quarto generates from each float's `{#tbl-...}` /

          // renders as the label and nothing else ("Table S1"), directly adjacent to the

          // outright with "no cross-reference placeholder pages found".
          //
          // A document-level include-in-header MERGES with the one in ms/_metadata.yml rather

          // references read "Table S1", not "Table S 1"). The condition keeps a real caption
          // rendering if one is ever added.
          // An "empty" caption is not `[]`: Quarto wraps it, and its repr is
          // `sequence([ ], block(body: [ ]), [ ])` (dumped from the render on 2026-08-27).
          // Comparing to `[]` therefore silently never matches and the rule looks broken.
          #show figure.caption: it => {
            if repr(it.body).contains("block(body: [ ])") { none } else { it }

<!-- This document compiles supplementary figures for the dementia EWAS manuscript. -->

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/demographics/output/followup_timeline_figure.png){#suppfig-timeline width="100%"}

::: {.rev}
**[@suppfig-timeline]** | **Timing of cognitive assessments and dementia surveillance by group.** Study design: blood for DNA methylation was drawn at the AGES-I baseline examination, and cognition was classified there and again at AGES-II; shaded columns span the first to last visit of each examination. MCI could therefore be diagnosed only at the examinations, whereas dementia was also ascertained from records until the end of surveillance (dashed line). Transition group: labels give cognitive status at AGES-I and, with the number of participants, at AGES-II for those whose group was established there. The other participants were assigned at AGES-I (prev_dementia) or from records: by the absence of a recorded dementia diagnosis in stable_normal and stable_mci, and by a recorded diagnosis in normal2incid and mci2incid. Gray lines mark the surveillance period; red bars span the 5th–95th percentiles of the dementia-diagnosis dates (circle, median). At right are the numbers assigned at AGES-II and from records, and the follow-up reported in Table 1, in years, as mean (SD); for normal2mci, and for stable_mci participants who attended AGES-II, it ends at AGES-II, although dementia surveillance continued. Groups are as in Table 1, where prev_dementia is labeled prev. AGES, Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study; MCI, mild cognitive impairment; n, number of participants; SD, standard deviation.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/dmp/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_5_manhattan.png){#suppfig-manhattan width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-manhattan]** | **Manhattan plot of genome-wide DNA methylation associations across dementia transitions.** The plot displays [−log~10~ *P*]{.rev} for CpG sites across chromosomes 1–22. Each point represents an individual CpG site. The red dashed horizontal line indicates the genome-wide significance threshold (*P* = [1.0]{.rev} × 10^−8^). Diamond-shaped markers highlight representative CpG sites exceeding this threshold, with colors indicating dementia transition types: normal to MCI (normal2mci), stable MCI (stable_mci), normal to incident dementia (normal2incid), MCI to incident dementia (mci2incid), and prevalent dementia (prev). Gene symbols for these CpG sites are annotated above the plot, together with potential neurological relevance inferred from their known gene functions.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/normal2mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_normal2incid_DMP.png){#suppfig-normal2incid_DMP width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-normal2incid_DMP]** | **Effect size comparison between normal2incid and other dementia transitions for genome-wide significant DMPs.** Scatter plots of effect sizes for the normal2incid transition (x-axis) against other transitions (y-axis) for differentially methylated positions (DMPs) at *P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^. Each point represents an individual CpG site, with blue lines indicating the linear regression fit. Spearman correlation coefficients (*r*) and [*P* values]{.rev} (in red) are shown for each comparison. A few CpG sites were removed as outliers. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/normal2mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_normal2incid_extended_DMP.png){#suppfig-normal2incid_extended_DMP width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-normal2incid_extended_DMP]** | **Effect size association with normal2incid transition for extended DMPs.** The effect size of normal2incid transition exhibits significant positive correlation with mci2incid transitions for the extended DMPs, i.e., the CpG sites that passed less stringent association thresholds of [1.0 × 10^−5^, 1.0 × 10^−6^, or 1.0 × 10^−7^]{.rev} (**A**), while it exhibits significant negative correlation with normal2mci transition for the extended DMPs (**B**). Each point represents an individual CpG site, with blue lines indicating the linear regression fit. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients [(*r*) and their corresponding *P* values]{.rev} (in red) are shown for each comparison. The number of extended DMPs is shown at the top under the indicated association threshold. A few CpG sites were removed as outliers. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group. *P* < 1.0 × 10^−300^ indicates a value below the double-precision machine limit.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/normal2mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_mci2incid_extended_DMP.png){#suppfig-mci2incid_extended_DMP width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-mci2incid_extended_DMP]** | **Effect size association with mci2incid transition for extended DMPs.** The effect size of mci2incid transition exhibits significant positive correlation with prevalent dementia for the extended DMPs, i.e., the CpG sites that passed less stringent association thresholds of [1.0 × 10^−5^, 1.0 × 10^−6^, or 1.0 × 10^−7^]{.rev} (**A**), while it exhibits significant negative correlation with normal2mci transition for the extended DMPs (**B**). Each point represents an individual CpG site, with blue lines indicating the linear regression fit. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients [(*r*) and their corresponding *P* values]{.rev} (in red) are shown for each comparison. The number of CpG sites (n) included in each analysis is indicated at the top of each panel under the specified association threshold. A few CpG sites were removed as outliers. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/normal2mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_ES_corr_mci2incid_normal2mci.png){#suppfig-ES_corr_mci2incid_normal2mci width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-ES_corr_mci2incid_normal2mci]** | **Effect size association with mci2incid and normal2mci transition.** [Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between the effect sizes of prevalent dementia (red), normal2incid (green) or stable_mci (blue) and those of the mci2incid or normal2mci transition, at 21 CpG selection thresholds. The x-axis gives the threshold *t* on the −log~10~ *P* scale: *t* = 0 includes all 799,149 CpG sites (no *P*-value filter), and each step of 0.5 keeps only the CpG sites with *P* < 1.0 × 10^−*t*^ in at least one of the five group contrasts, up to *t* = 10 (95 CpG sites). Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/stable_mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_stable_mci_DMP.png){#suppfig-stable_mci_DMP width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-stable_mci_DMP]** | **Effect size comparison between stable_mci and other dementia transitions for genome-wide significant DMPs.** Scatter plots of effect sizes for the stable MCI group (x-axis) against the other transitions (y-axis) for differentially methylated positions (DMPs) at *P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^. The 403 DMPs separate into a main group (n = 343) and an outlier group (n = 60), the latter defined by a strongly negative stable_mci effect size (< −0.2). Each point represents an individual CpG site, with lines indicating the linear regression fit within each group. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients (*r*) and their corresponding [*P* values]{.rev} are shown along each fitted line. The outlier group shows no significant correlation with any other transition. A few extreme CpG sites were excluded from the display. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/stable_mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_stable_mci_extended_prev.png){#suppfig-stable_mci_extended_prev width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_prev]** | **Effect size association between stable_mci and prevalent dementia for extended DMPs.** The effect size of the stable MCI group exhibits a significant positive correlation with prevalent dementia for the main group of extended DMPs, i.e., the CpG sites that passed less stringent association thresholds of [1.0 × 10^−5^, 1.0 × 10^−6^, or 1.0 × 10^−7^]{.rev}, whereas the outlier group (stable_mci effect size < −0.2) shows no correlation at any threshold. Each point represents an individual CpG site, with lines indicating the linear regression fit within each group. The number of CpG sites (n) included in each analysis is indicated at the top of each panel under the specified association threshold. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients (*r*) and their corresponding [*P* values]{.rev} are shown [for the main and outlier groups in the lower left of each panel]{.rev}. A few extreme CpG sites were excluded from the display. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/stable_mci_focused/patch_figures/output/fig_sup_stable_mci_extended_transitions.png){#suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions]** | **Effect size association between stable_mci and the other dementia transitions for extended DMPs.** As in [@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_prev], but comparing the stable MCI effect size against the normal2incid (**A**), mci2incid (**B**) and normal2mci (**C**) transitions for the CpG sites that passed less stringent association thresholds of [1.0 × 10^−5^, 1.0 × 10^−6^, or 1.0 × 10^−7^]{.rev}. The main group correlates significantly with every transition at every threshold, whereas the outlier group (stable_mci effect size < −0.2) does not. Each point represents an individual CpG site, with lines indicating the linear regression fit within each group. The number of CpG sites (n) included in each analysis is indicated at the top of each panel under the specified association threshold. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients (*r*) and their corresponding [*P* values]{.rev} are shown [for the main and outlier groups in the lower left of each panel]{.rev}. [Effect size is ΔM, the covariate-adjusted difference in mean M-value between a group and the stable normal group.]{.rev}

![](/VAE_UMAP_comb/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_vae_methodology.png){#suppfig-vae-methodology width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-vae-methodology]** | **Methodology of the regularized Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for methylation embedding.** **A,** Schematic representation of the deep generative model architecture. The encoder network reduces input dimensionality through four dense layers (512, 256, 128, 64 units), each with batch normalization, ReLU activation, and dropout (0.05–0.1). The probabilistic latent space captures a 6-dimensional representation using $z_{mean}$ and $z_{log\_var}$ parameters with the reparameterization trick ($\beta = 0.001$). The symmetric decoder reconstructs the original methylation patterns. **B,** [5-fold cross-validation. The 2,491 participants were split into five folds (497–499 each), with stratification on dementia transition category requested. In each iteration, four folds were used to train the VAE, and the held-out fold served as validation data for early stopping and learning-rate reduction. The final embedding is the average, dimension by dimension, of the five models' latent means ($z_{mean}$) for all participants.]{.rev}

The remaining four dimensions did not reach significance and are not shown.

![](/VAE_UMAP_comb/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_vae_null_distribution.png){#suppfig-vae-null-dist width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-vae-null-dist]** | **VAE null distribution of DPS at THR8.** Permutation-based null distributions for DPS across VAE dimension pairs at threshold *P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^ (403 CpGs). Vertical lines indicate observed DPS values. Permutation [*P* values]{.rev} assess whether observed trajectory scores exceed those expected under random shuffling, which breaks the linkage between dementia transition categories and CpG site methylation.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/VAE_UMAP_comb/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_umap_null_distribution.png){#suppfig-umap-null-dist width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-umap-null-dist]** | **UMAP null distribution of DPS at THR8.** Permutation-based null distributions for DPS across UMAP dimension pairs at threshold *P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^ (403 CpGs). Vertical lines indicate observed DPS values. Layout identical to @suppfig-vae-null-dist. [*P* < 0.001 indicates that none of the 1,000 permutations reached the observed DPS.]{.rev}

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/VAE_UMAP_comb/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_perm_heatmap.png){#suppfig-perm-heatmap width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-perm-heatmap]** | **Permutation [*P* values]{.rev} for the dementia progression score (DPS) of every latent dimension pair.** Each cell gives the empirical [*P* value]{.rev} — the fraction of 1,000 permutations whose DPS equalled or exceeded the observed value — printed to three decimals[, or as < 0.001 where none of the 1,000 permutations reached the observed value]{.rev}. [Tile fill shades from light salmon at the smallest *P* values, close to the color at the *P* = 0.05 significance threshold, to white at *P* = 1]{.rev}; the cell number is printed in white where the pair is significant (*P* < 0.05) and in black where it is not (*P* ≥ 0.05). Rows are the 15 dimension pairs (e.g., dim_1 vs dim_2), where dim_1 corresponds to UMAP_1 in the UMAP columns and VAE_1 in the VAE columns; the four columns are the UMAP and VAE methods at THR7 (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−7^) and THR8 (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^).

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/APOE/patch_figures/output/fig_suppl_apoe_boxplot.png){#suppfig-apoe-boxplot-t7 width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-apoe-boxplot-t7]** | **APOE genotype effects on methylation-derived latent dimensions at THR7 (949 CpGs).** Boxplots showing the distribution of the five latent dimensions that differed significantly by APOE functional role (UMAP_2, UMAP_1, UMAP_3, VAE_1, VAE_2; Kruskal-Wallis *P* < 0.05) across six APOE genotypes (ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3, ε3/ε3, ε2/ε4, ε3/ε4, ε4/ε4) in 2,487 [participants]{.rev}, arranged in a 1 × 5 grid. Genotypes are grouped by functional role: Protective (ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3), Neutral (ε3/ε3), and Detrimental (ε2/ε4, ε3/ε4, ε4/ε4), indicated by color-coded background bars. Kruskal-Wallis test [*P* values,]{.rev} computed across the three functional role groups, are shown in red at the top of each panel; orange annotations indicate median values for each genotype.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/pathway_analysis/01_genes/output/fig_sup_pval_with_top_genes_plot.png){#suppfig-pval-with-top-genes width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-pval-with-top-genes]** | **Statistical significance distribution of top-ranked CpG sites across dementia transitions.** For each dementia transition, CpG sites are ranked by association strength (−log~10~ [*P*)]{.rev} and the top 2,000 sites are plotted. Red diamonds highlight the 1st, 1,000th, and 2,000th ranked CpG sites with their −log~10~ [*P* values]{.rev} annotated. The dashed blue line indicates the genome-wide significance threshold (*P* = 1.0 × 10^−8^), with the number of CpG sites exceeding this threshold shown in blue text.

![](/pathway_analysis/05_patch_fig_and_make_table/output/fig_sup_upset_top2000_genes_and_GO_terms.png){#suppfig-upset-top2000 width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-upset-top2000]** | **Overlap analysis of genes and GO terms for the top 2,000 CpG sites across dementia transitions.** **A.** UpSet plot showing the intersection of genes associated with the top 2,000 CpG sites across dementia transitions. The left bars show the total number of genes for each transition, while the vertical bars show the size of gene intersections, with connected dots below indicating which transitions contribute to each intersection; intersections of fewer than 110 genes are not shown. **B.** UpSet plot depicting the overlap of significantly enriched Gene Ontology (GO) biological process terms across transitions. As in panel A, the left bars indicate the total number of terms per transition and the vertical bars the size of term intersections; intersections of fewer than 5 terms are not shown[, and parent terms whose genes were identical to those of a significant child term were removed (see Methods)]{.rev}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](/pathway_analysis/05_patch_fig_and_make_table/output/fig_sup_barplot_top2000_function_categorization.png){#suppfig-barplot-top2000 width="100%"}

**[@suppfig-barplot-top2000]** | **[Distribution of biological function categories among GO terms significant in only one group, top 2,000 CpG sites.]{.rev}** [The barplot shows the distribution of functional categories among the Gene Ontology (GO) terms significant in only one group, for each dementia transition. Terms were assigned to functional categories by keyword rules and counted by their redundancy-aware weights (see Methods); categories with a weighted count below two in a group are not shown.]{.rev} Bar heights represent the percentage of GO terms in each dementia transition for a functional category, with numbers above bars indicating the [weighted]{.rev} count of GO terms in that category. [The categories named in the Results for the top 1,000 CpG sites recur in the same groups, but not all remain specific to one group (for example, cell-cycle regulation also appears in stable_mci).]{.rev}
